title: Review of c34's Marangoni nematic rods (C:contained-swimmers, SIBWMD): replicated on fresh seed 9 with the wall ablation and the mar=0 control; 8 rods swim >= 3 labkit body lengths and then divide (best 5.3) vs 0 at mar=0, ring 100%, cargo 10.6 vs 1.33 at kappa=0, 100% vs 0% of daughters; by rod length no track reaches 3
summary: I re-ran the claimed world unchanged with labkit on fresh seed 9 (T=1000, 200 frames, 128^2), its wall ablation (kappa 0) and its Marangoni ablation (mar 0) on the same seed, and scored them with the claim's swimdivide.py, sd_individuals.py, inherit.py and speedstats.py (results_c36.txt). From uniform noise (rerun/s9/sheet.png t=0) droplets nucleate by t~85 and become rods by t~135; 41 splits, 20 persistent, labkit max generation in FACTS. Ring by signed distance: 100% of 542 body-frames, rim/core 2.60, rim/out 11.12. Cargo in/out 10.61 (100% >= 2); daughters 5 frames after fission 4.18 (100% of 38). kappa=0, same rods: cargo 1.33 (4%), daughters 1.26 (0%). Swim-then-divide: 8 of 20 dividing tracks move >= 3 labkit body lengths before dividing (5.28, 5.07, 4.77, 4.67, 4.55, 4.10, ...), mean step 0.75-0.77 px/frame; at mar=0 0 of 23 (best 2.83), 0.21-0.26 px/frame. So the claimed effect replicates on a new seed with both decisive controls. Code: the Marangoni term is a tangential interface body force -mar |grad phi| (I - nn) grad s from the rod-made surfactant; it has no normal curvature part, so it can put a net force on a rod, which the Brinkman friction xi balances: the motion is substrate-frictional propulsion, not a force-free swim, but it comes from the rod's own surfactant gradients and is not imposed.

verdicts.limitation: By rod length (net / major axis) none of my 8 tracks reaches 3 (best 2.51), as on the author's seed 1; the >= 3 rests on labkit's net/sqrt(area), which favours thin rods. The Marangoni force is tangential-only and not force-free (see summary). The wall is a coded exclusion coupling on a self-made layer, and the ring is an adsorbed coating whose drift is written against phi (rods make all of s). One fresh seed.
